label: produces
notes: Repointed from METPO:2000202 by TraitMech#329. The gate encodes the split with RO:0002234 (has output) on BOTH sides, because spelling it only as a subject_types exclusion of the three activity node types was not a faithful proxy: observation.yaml's 'assay or measurement process' was typed EXPERIMENTAL_FACTOR and so routed around that exclusion onto this chemical-production term, which is exactly the has-output case the split exists to divert. That node is an investigation process by its own description and is now typed BIOLOGICAL_PROCESS, its edge moved to RO:0002234, and neither subject_types nor object_types admits EXPERIMENTAL_FACTOR any more. subject_types no longer admits CHEMICAL: a chemical does not bring another entity into existence the way an agent does. Two such edges moved to RO:0001001 (derives into) in #327 and the last one, acetyl_phosphate -> ATP, was remodelled onto an explicit acetate kinase step in #331, so the gate now matches the definition exactly.

label: uses electron donor
notes: METPO:2000008/2000009 are rdfs:subPropertyOf METPO:2000001, whose rdfs:domain is METPO:1000525 (microbe), so a non-organism subject entails that subject IS a microbe. CausalNodeTypeEnum has no organism member, so no causal-graph edge can satisfy the domain and the label is never grounded here (#295). The 15 edges that carried it were moved to <chemical> RO:0002327 <trait>; that form is NOT settled - RO:0002327's range is 'biological process or activity', so a TRAIT object is its own violation (#302), and collapsing donor and acceptor onto one relation loses the distinction (#303). Prefer the graph's BIOLOGICAL_PROCESS node as the object until #302 lands; see docs/CURATION_PLAYBOOK.md. The organism-subject form stays valid at the assertion site, which is what the OBJECT_PROPERTY records' domain: describes.

Used for the 103 #301 edges whose subject IS an activity; the rest of the produces family takes METPO:2007800 (proposals/metpo_traitmech_v9) because a protein, trait or chemical subject cannot satisfy this domain. subject_types is gated to the three CausalNodeTypeEnum values that are activities, so a protein-subject edge is refused here rather than silently re-acquiring the same class of domain violation this migration exists to remove.

label: derives into
notes: biolink:derives_into (exact_mapping RO:0001001) holds between two material entities where the new begins to exist as the old ceases and inherits the significant portion of its matter - i.e. substrate-to-product chemistry. Used for the disproportionation pair (thiosulfate -> sulfate and -> sulfide), which previously sat on `produces` with a CHEMICAL subject: a chemical does not bring another into existence the way an agent does. METPO:2007405 (oxidized to, proposals v2) was considered for the sulfate half and rejected - it fits only the oxidised half, splitting a matched pair from one reaction, and it is an unminted placeholder where RO:0001001 is real. RO:0001001 declares no domain, so no causal node type is excluded (#327).

label: is hydrolyzed to
notes: Substrate-to-product hydrolysis: cellulose -> cellobiose. Grounded to RO:0001001 rather than METPO:2000013 (hydrolyzes), which reads agent-to-substrate, so the previous grounding asserted that cellulose hydrolyses cellobiose (#327). closeMatch not exactMatch because the corpus label names the mechanism (hydrolysis) while RO:0001001 is the general transformation relation; the label is kept for that extra specificity. This is the last of the 366 #301 edges.

label: has input
notes: biolink gives has input domain 'biological process or activity' and range 'named thing', the inverse companion of RO:0002234 already used here. subject_types is gated to the three activity node types for the same reason has output is: a non-activity subject cannot satisfy the domain. Added in #331 to model the acetate kinase step explicitly rather than asserting that a chemical produces ATP.
